segments.tts: When was AI first mentioned? Spoiler: way before ChatGPT.

August 31st, 1955. A young mathematician, John McCarthy, writes a funding proposal with Marvin Minsky, Nathaniel Rochester and Claude Shannon. And right in the title: a brand-new term – artificial intelligence.
The plan: a two-month, ten-person summer workshop at Dartmouth College in 1956. Their bold idea: every feature of intelligence can be described so precisely that a machine could simulate it.
But the question is even older. In 1950, Alan Turing asked: "Can machines think?" – and proposed the imitation game, today's Turing test.
Seventy-one years later, that idea fits in your pocket.
